t0: A release is the thing that is versioned, cleared, promoted from Airfield to Airfield and reported on: a commit, a tag, notes, Cargo and the image digests its Sortie built.
t1: A release starts as a draft of a commit, with notes written from the changes since the last one. Publishing it makes the tag and fixes it: from then on only withdrawing it is possible.
t2: Make it from (a branch, tag or commit; empty is the default branch)
t3: Read from the changes since the last release. You choose.
t4: Write the notes from the pull requests and commits since the last release
t5: A draft: nothing is tagged yet, and the notes and files can still change.
t6: A candidate: it may go to Airfields that are not protected, for testing, but it is not released.
t7: Published: its version, commit, tag, Cargo and image digests never change. A correction is a new release.
t8: none: this release carries no image
t9: The notes were written again from the changes.
t10: Write them again from the changes
t11: Build once, promote the same thing: a promotion starts the pipeline at this tag with this version and image digest. Each Airfield has its own checklist.
t12: Its notes and files are removed. A candidate or published release is never deleted.
t13: Propose the changelog as a pull request
t14: This is the latest release. Its address stays the same for the next one: use
t15: No files or images are attached.
t16: Files and images of this release, with where each came from
t17: Attach what a Sortie built (its {run} id)
t18: Files and images are fixed once a release is published, each with the checksum it had.
t19: This address is too long for a QR code. Copy it instead:
t20: A phone that is not signed in is asked to sign in first.
t21: Point the phone's camera at the code to download
t22: Point the phone's camera at the code to open this release, where each file has its own download.
t23: Anyone with the address may download it.
t24: A phone that is not signed in is sent to sign in and then back to the download.
t25: Android asks once to allow installing from the browser it was downloaded with.
t27: (an existing tag at that commit is adopted) and fixes the release. Its notes, files, tag and image digests can never change; if something is wrong, withdraw it and make a new release.
t28: Allow downloading its files without signing in (only where the installation and the {project} allow it)
t29: It stays in the record, marked as withdrawn with your reason, and is no longer promoted or offered for download. What already runs is not touched: return that Airfield to base if it should go back.
